name: Salesforce (core platform)
scope_notes: API availability depends on edition. Creation of Connected Apps is restricted from Spring ’26; assess External Client Apps for new integrations.

controls.name: Permitted Users: Admin approved users are pre-authorized
controls.what: Only users whose profile or permission set is assigned to the connected app can use it; others are refused.
controls.setting: Setup > Connected Apps > Manage > Edit Policies > Permitted Users; Metadata ConnectedAppOauthPolicy isAdminApproved (ECA: permittedUsersPolicyType=AdminApprovedPreAuthorized)
controls.quote: If set to true , only users with the appropriate profile or permission set can access the app. These users don’t have to approve the app before they can access it.

controls.name: API Access Control (Allow only admin-approved apps)
controls.what: Org-wide: only connected apps installed or approved by an admin can call the Salesforce API; a separate switch covers customer/partner users.
controls.setting: Metadata ConnectedAppSettings enableAdminApprovedAppsOnly / enableAdminApprovedAppsOnlyForExternalUser; Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage (install/unblock)
controls.plan: Must be enabled by Salesforce Customer Support
controls.quote: If true , only apps that have been approved or installed by the admin can call the Salesforce API. To access this field, you must contact Salesforce Customer Support to enable API Access Control.

controls.name: IP Relaxation
controls.what: Enforce (default) applies org and profile IP restrictions to the app; Bypass options relax them, and Enforce_RelaxRefresh skips them for refresh-token exchanges.
controls.setting: Connected app / external client app OAuth policies > IP Relaxation; Metadata ipRelaxation (ECA ipRelaxationPolicyType)
controls.quote: ENFORCE (default)—Enforces the IP restrictions configured for the org, such as the IP ranges assigned to a user profile.

controls.name: Profile Login IP Ranges
controls.what: Restricts the IP ranges from which users of a profile, including API integration users, can log in.
controls.setting: Setup > Profiles > [profile] > Login IP Ranges; Metadata Profile.loginIpRanges
controls.quote: The list of IP address ranges from which users with a particular profile can log in.

controls.name: Enforce login IP ranges on every request
controls.what: Checks profile Login IP Ranges on every request, including from client apps, not only at login.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SecuritySettings/SessionSettings enforceIpRangesEveryRequest
controls.quote: If true , the IP addresses in Login IP Ranges are enforced when a user accesses Salesforce (on every page request), including access from a client app.

controls.name: Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated
controls.what: Binds a session to the IP it was created from.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SessionSettings lockSessionsToIp
controls.quote: Indicates whether user sessions are locked to the IP address from which the user logged in ( true ) or not ( false ).

controls.name: Refresh Token Policy
controls.what: Sets refresh tokens to valid until revoked (default), immediately expire, expire after a fixed time, or expire after inactivity.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth policies > Refresh Token Policy; Metadata refreshTokenPolicy (ECA refreshTokenPolicyType)
controls.quote: infinite —The refresh token is used indefinitely, unless revoked by the user or Salesforce admin. Default setting.

controls.name: Connected app session timeout
controls.what: Sets how long an access token session from the app lasts; falls back to profile then org session timeout.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > Timeout Value; Metadata ConnectedAppSessionPolicy sessionTimeout
controls.quote: If you don’t set a value, Salesforce uses the timeout value in the connected app user’s profile.

controls.name: High assurance session required (Block / Raise session level)
controls.what: Requires MFA-level sessions for the app; flows without a user approval step, such as JWT bearer, are blocked.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > High assurance session required; Metadata sessionLevel/policyAction
controls.quote: For flows without a user approval step, API logins with the High Assurance session security level are blocked.

controls.name: Enable Client Credentials Flow + Run As user
controls.what: Client credentials flow is off unless an admin enables it per app and names an API Only execution user whose access the tokens carry.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth policies > Enable Client Credentials Flow, Run As; Metadata isClientCredentialEnabled + oauthClientCredentialUser
controls.quote: Salesforce returns access tokens on behalf of this user. This user must have the API Only permission.

controls.name: Block OAuth username-password and user-agent flows
controls.what: Org-wide switches that block the OAuth username-password flow and the user-agent flow.
controls.setting: Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings; Metadata OauthOidcSettings blockOAuthUnPwFlow / blockOAuthUsrAgtFlow
controls.quote: Indicates whether the username-password flow is blocked ( true ) or not blocked ( false ). The default value is false .

controls.name: Require PKCE for authorization code flows
controls.what: Requires PKCE on all supported variants of the authorization code flow into the org.
controls.setting: Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings; Metadata OauthOidcSettings isPkceRequired
controls.quote: This setting requires PKCE for all supported variations of the authorization code flow, including the web server flow, the Authorization Code and Credentials Flow, and their derivatives.

controls.name: Enable Token Exchange Flow
controls.what: Token exchange is off unless enabled on the connected app or external client app.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth settings > Enable Token Exchange Flow; Metadata isTokenExchangeEnabled (ECA isTokenExchangeFlowEnabled)
controls.quote: If set to true , the connected app can use the OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow to exchange tokens from an external identity provider for Salesforce tokens.

controls.name: Require secret for token exchange
controls.what: Requires the app's consumer secret on token exchange requests.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth settings; Metadata isSecretRequiredForTokenExchange
controls.quote: If set to true , the connected app must include its consumer secret ( client_secret ) in the token request during the OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow.

controls.name: Token exchange handler enablement
controls.what: The handler must be enabled and bound to specific apps with an execution user; it validates external tokens and maps users.
controls.setting: Setup > Token Exchange Handlers; Metadata OauthTokenExchangeHandler isEnabled + enablements
controls.quote: The enablement settings for the token exchange handler, including the execution user who runs the Apex class, the connected apps or external client apps for which it’s enabled

controls.name: Connected app creation restricted (Spring '26)
controls.what: New connected apps cannot be created without contacting Support; existing apps keep working and external client apps are recommended.
controls.setting: Platform default; contact Salesforce Support to re-enable
controls.quote: Connected apps creation is restricted as of Spring ‘26. You can use existing connected apps during and after Spring ‘26.

controls.name: External client app JWT access token timeout
controls.what: For ECAs issuing JWT-based access tokens, sets a custom expiry (1 minute to 12 hours) instead of the session timeout.
controls.quote: the amount of time before a JWT-based access token issued to a named user expires. Values are in minutes.

controls.name: Consumer secret access via REST API
controls.what: Controls whether external client app consumer secrets can be read through the credentials REST API.
controls.quote: Indicates whether OAuth consumer secrets can be accessed through the credentials REST API ( true ) or not ( false ).

controls.name: Block (Connected Apps OAuth Usage)
controls.what: Blocking a connected app ends all current sessions for it and prevents new ones until unblocked.
controls.setting: Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Block

authentication.summary: The client POSTs a token from an external identity provider (access, refresh or ID token, SAML assertion or JWT) to the Salesforce token endpoint. An Apex token exchange handler validates it and maps it to a Salesforce user, and Salesforce returns its own access token.

federation.details: This path exists to exchange an external IdP token for Salesforce tokens. Trust is defined in customer-written Apex: the handler decides what counts as a valid token and which user it maps to, and it can create users.

ip_restriction.boundary: General Salesforce controls apply to OAuth apps: profile login IP ranges, the app's IP relaxation policy, and optional 'Enforce login IP ranges on every request'. The IP relaxation and continuous-enforcement pages do not name the token exchange flow, so how its initial exchange is treated was not established.

lifetime.summary: Salesforce access token follows session timeout (inactivity); default 2 h

renewal.summary: If the app requests one, Salesforce returns a refresh token governed by the app's refresh token policy (valid until revoked, immediate, idle or fixed expiry); otherwise the client exchanges a fresh external token.

administration.summary: Admins create a token exchange handler (Apex class plus OauthTokenExchangeHandler metadata), enable it for specific connected apps or external client apps, and pick a Run As execution user. Requested scopes must be a subset of the app's scopes; external client apps can require a client secret for the exchange.
administration.conditions: Available in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer Editions. Validation and user mapping are customer code, so security depends on the handler implementation.

sso.details: Issuance requires a token from the external identity provider; no Salesforce UI login or MFA step is described.

offboard.details: Opaque tokens stop on deactivation of the mapped user; JWT-based access tokens stay valid until timeout.
